subject: Money
title: Political Power
description: Learn Political Power in one minute.

hook.text: In the 2020 U.S. election cycle, the top 100 donors gave more than the bottom 4.75 million donors combined.

buildup.text: Campaign contributions, lobbying, and think tank funding give the wealthy outsized influence over policy.

discovery.text: Princeton research found U.S. policy reflects wealthy preferences. Average citizens' views have near-zero impact.

twist.text: Citizens United (2010) allowed unlimited corporate spending on elections. Money became speech. Literally.

climax.text: Economic inequality becomes political inequality. Those with the most money shape the rules that protect their wealth.

punchline.text: One person, one vote. One dollar, one voice.

quiz.question: What did Princeton research find about U.S. policy?
options: It reflects wealthy preferences; average citizens have near-zero impact
